name: decatenator
short_description: CLI tool that extracts code blocks from Markdown files with file path headings into real source files.
long_description: DeCatenator (decat) is a command-line utility that unpacks code embedded in Markdown files into actual source files on disk. It reads Markdown level-2 or level-3 headings that contain file paths and extracts the accompanying code blocks (either fenced or unfenced) to write files on disk. This is the inverse operation of the Catenator tool. It supports both fenced code blocks (triple backticks) and unfenced content, automatically creates parent directories, and can read from files or stdin. The tool is useful for extracting code examples from documentation, literate programming workflows, or code embedded in markdown notes.

modules.name: _core
modules.description: Core parsing and file writing logic with functions to extract code blocks from Markdown lines and write them to disk.

modules.name: cli
modules.description: Command-line interface entry point that handles argument parsing and pipes input through the core extraction functions.

modules.name: __init__
modules.description: Package initialization that re-exports core functions and manages version information from package metadata.

modules.name: test_core
modules.description: Comprehensive test suite covering extraction of fenced/unfenced code blocks, directory creation, mixed formats, and edge cases.
